requirements.text: The TCS shall support 5 levels of UAV interaction: receipt/transmission of data, direct receipt of data, control of payload, control of UAV less launch/recovery, and full control including launch/recovery.
The TCS shall provide mission planning, mission control and monitoring, payload product management, targeting, and C4I system interface functions.
The TCS shall be interoperable with Predator and Outrider UAVs and their associated payloads.
The TCS shall provide a graphical user interface for mission planning, including waypoint definition on a map display.
The TCS shall be capable of entering DII-COE compliant networks and interfacing with specified C4I systems.
The TCS shall provide the capability to process, display, and perform limited exploitation of EO, IR, and SAR payload imagery.
The TCS shall provide fault detection/location (FD/L) to the LRU level.
The TCS shall initialize to the Operations State within 60 seconds from power-on in Normal Startup Mode.
The TCS shall resume the Operations State within 45 seconds in Recovery Startup Mode.
The TCS shall be capable of storing a minimum of 500 mission plans.
The TCS shall be capable of storing up to 24 hours of payload data.
The TCS shall be Year 2000 compliant.
The TCS shall meet security requirements in accordance with DoD Directive 5200.28(D) for Automated Information Systems.
The TCS shall restrict access to software upgrade and parameter modification capabilities via password protection.
The TCS shall be designed such that no single hardware failure or software error results in an unsafe command to the air vehicle.
The TCS shall provide a common Human-Computer Interface (HCI) to simplify user operations and training across different UAV types.
The TCS shall be scaleable and modular to meet varying Service deployment requirements.
